clue.text: Political skill, say, shown by Conservative crowd

parts.note: to say is to state
a raft is a large number or crowd of things

explanation.surface: A Tory mob shows off its talent for politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Statecraft is the art of conducting government affairs, a skill in politics.

clue.text: Man who's taken up patent right

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: patent means obvious, open, overt

explanation.surface: A man has picked up an obvious entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Trevor is a man's first name, so it is an example of a man.

clue.text: Sturdily built saw's beginning to cut into wood

indicators.note: the letter is placed so that it slices into the middle of the other word

parts.note: a thicket is a dense small wood

indicators.note: the beginning of the word saw's is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A stocky woodcutter's saw starts biting into the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw's' reads as the tool in a wood-cutting picture, but only its first letter is used, and 'to cut into' means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thickset has a heavy, solid, stocky frame.

clue.text: Court studies one account of events

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
I is the Roman numeral one
a story is a narrative account of events

explanation.surface: A judge examines a single version of what happened.
explanation.definitionFit: A consistory is a church court or council, such as the Pope's assembly of cardinals.

clue.text: In addition to staff, I introduced robot

parts.note: and means in addition to

indicators.note: introduced means brought in, so the letter is put inside the other word

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Besides the workers, I brought in a mechanical helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced' puts I inside ROD, giving ROID.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a robot built to look like a human.

clue.text: Takes advantage of call from the military

definitions.meaning: to tap a resource is to exploit or draw on it
the bugle call played at a military funeral or for lights out

explanation.definitionFit: Taps means exploits a source, and is also the US army bugle call at day's end.

clue.text: Eighteen, of course, on the wagon

definitions.meaning: a golf course has eighteen tees, so the tee count in total is eighteen
on the wagon means abstaining from alcohol

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a golfing joke: a golf course has eighteen holes, each starting from a tee, so the sum of tees is eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotal person drinks no alcohol, which is what being on the wagon means.

clue.text: Coin two boys found in mint

parts.note: a penny is a coin
Roy is a boy's name
Al is another boy's name

explanation.surface: A coin and two lads turn up at the Royal Mint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two boys' gives two names, ROY and AL; the surface makes 'mint' the place coins are made, but it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennyroyal is a species of plant in the mint family, used as a herb.

clue.text: Charge involving drink without support

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the drink goes around the support

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
a leg is a support, as of a table

explanation.surface: A charge of drinking without anything to lean on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'involving' merely links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to claim or accuse, as in bringing a charge against someone.

clue.text: Gave up place for patient

definitions.meaning: to give up one's place or post is to quit it formally
patient here means accepting what comes without complaint

explanation.definitionFit: Resigned means stepped down from a post, and also calmly accepting one's lot.

clue.text: Influential Russian mixing up tsarina endlessly

indicators.note: mixing means the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of tsarina is dropped

explanation.surface: A powerful Russian confuses the Empress, cutting her off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TSARINA to TSARIN; 'mixing' rearranges UP + TSARIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasputin was the mystic who held great sway over the last Russian imperial family.

clue.text: Part of body that may be offensive

definitions.meaning: limbs attached at the shoulders, the clue being in the singular as a body part

explanation.definitionFit: Arms are upper limbs, and also weapons, which may be offensive in the military sense.

clue.text: Article's only been edited for queen

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: edited means the letters are revised into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor reworks a short item for a royal story.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Boleyn was the second wife of Henry VIII and Queen of England.

clue.text: Change on script party put in — who did it?

indicators.note: put in means the party is inserted into the rearranged letters
change means the letters that follow are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone altered the script and added a party scene; who was responsible?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' signals an anagram of ON SCRIPT and 'put in' an insertion; the question 'who did it?' defines the person who altered the script.
explanation.definitionFit: A media adviser who twists a story is exactly the person who changes the script.

clue.text: Girl goes on the links — Alice found 'it too hot to do

definitions.text: Alice found 'it too hot to do

indicators.note: goes on means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: Daisy is a girl's name
a chain is a series of links

explanation.surface: A girl heads for the golf links, but Alice thought it too warm to bother.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, Alice considers making a daisy chain but the hot day makes her sleepy. 'the links' looks like a golf course but is a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a garland of flowers is the task Carroll's heroine wondered about on that sleepy summer afternoon.

clue.text: No charge for this particular sort of bomb?

definitions.meaning: a subatomic particle with no electric charge
a nuclear weapon designed to kill by radiation; particular hints at particle

explanation.definitionFit: The neutron is the uncharged particle in an atom's nucleus, and also names a radiation bomb.

clue.text: More people in limited Gilbert and Sullivan production?

definitions.text: More people in limited Gilbert and Sullivan production?

parts.words: More people in limited Gilbert and Sullivan production?
parts.note: Thomas More wrote of an ideal island, and Gilbert and Sullivan wrote an operetta named after it, Limited; its people are both More's and theirs

explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is Sir Thomas More, author of Utopia; Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera is 'Utopia, Limited'. 'More' and 'limited' pose as ordinary words.
explanation.definitionFit: The inhabitants of an ideal imagined state, the island of More's book and of the comic opera.

clue.text: Show opening in December is dramatic production

indicators.note: the opening in a word is its first letter

parts.note: a play is a dramatic production

explanation.surface: A December show is a theatrical production.
explanation.definitionFit: To display is to show or exhibit something.

clue.text: Lavish incentive given to one girl

parts.note: a prod is a nudge or incentive
I is the Roman numeral one
gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: A generous nudge is offered to a single young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal means wastefully extravagant, spending freely.

clue.text: She had a lot of problems with her chest

definitions.text: She had a lot of problems with her chest

parts.words: She had a lot of problems with her chest
parts.note: a figure of Greek myth whose box (chest) released all the world's troubles, not a woman with bronchitis

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a medical complaint, but the chest is a box from Greek myth that let all evils into the world when opened.
explanation.definitionFit: The first woman in Greek myth, who opened the jar or box releasing all ills.

clue.text: Red Queen is mixed up and drunk

definitions.meaning: the nickname of Mary I of England for her burning of Protestants, red with blood
a cocktail of vodka and tomato juice, mixed and then drunk

explanation.definitionFit: The bloodthirsty Tudor monarch Mary I, and a vodka-and-tomato cocktail.

clue.text: Stone in ring given to mate

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
pal is a friend or mate

explanation.surface: A gem set in a ring is given to a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is an iridescent gemstone.

clue.text: Reluctant protest over extremists in senate

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to protest is to declare solemnly, to aver

indicators.note: the extremists in a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An unwilling objection raised over the radicals in the Senate.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means opposed or disinclined, unwilling.

clue.text: Secure in unusually idle position?

indicators.note: in means the first piece goes inside the second
unusually means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: sure means secure, safe

explanation.surface: Someone sits secure in an unusually idle post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' signals an anagram of IDLE (LEID) and 'in' an insertion; the whole clue describes a person of leisure, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being leisured means having ample free time, safely settled in an idle life.

clue.text: Attachment to sail mariner tries to avoid

definitions.meaning: a section of a sail that can be rolled or tied up to reduce its area
a ridge of rock or coral near the surface, dangerous to ships

explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a reducible strip of sail, and also a hidden rocky hazard for sailors.

clue.text: Old soldier gets year in glasshouse

parts.note: a ranger is a soldier, as in the US Army Rangers

explanation.surface: An old soldier gets a year in the glasshouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glasshouse' is British slang for a military prison, which fits the soldier surface, but here it is a greenhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a greenhouse built for growing citrus trees.

clue.text: Better option for an American

definitions.meaning: a bettor's multiple wager on four selections
a nickname for someone from the United States

explanation.definitionFit: A Yankee is a combination bet of eleven wagers, and also a US citizen.

clue.text: Talked rubbish, like Kipling's fools

definitions.meaning: Kipling mocked the cricketers as fools in white woollen trousers

explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem 'The Islanders' sneers at 'the flannelled fools at the wicket', cricketers in white flannel trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: To waffle or bluff is the sense of the verb, and cricketers were dressed in woollen cloth.
